title: Concrete Contractor Marketing: What Works in 2026
desc: Concrete contractor marketing that works in 2026: Google profile, job photos, neighbour cards, builder work, ads and seasonal timing, with sums and scripts.

blocks.h1: Concrete contractor marketing, *one slab at a time.*
blocks.lede: Good concrete contractor marketing is mostly about being easy to find and easy to trust: a Google Business Profile set to concrete contractor, a website with a page for each type of job, and lots of photos of finished local work. Then work the cheap sources most crews skip, like the neighbours around every pour, builders and landscapers, and past customers. Plan around the weather, and judge any paid ads by cost per signed job, not cost per lead.

blocks.html:
What is the best marketing for a concrete contractor?

Concrete is a visual trade with big tickets. A homeowner spending thousands on a driveway or a stamped patio wants to see that you have done one like it, near them, and that it still looks good. So the best concrete contractor marketing shows finished work to the right people at the moment they are ready to pour.

Here is the short list, in the order we would do it:

  1. Set up your Google Business Profile properly. Main category "Concrete contractor", every town you cover, and real job photos every week.
  2. Build a website with one page per job type. Driveways, patios, stamped and decorative concrete, footings and slabs, repairs, commercial flatwork.
  3. Photograph every job. Before, during the pour, the finish and the clean site.
  4. Ask for a review on the day you strip the forms or hand over.
  5. Work the street around every job. Your truck and crew on the street are the advert.
  6. Get on the list of builders, landscapers and pool companies.
  7. Add paid ads only once the basics are in place, and track the cost per signed job.

None of this needs a big budget. It needs a routine.

How do concrete contractors show up on Google?

Most residential concrete searches are local: "concrete driveway near me", "stamped concrete patio [town]", "concrete contractors [suburb]". The map results come from your Google Business Profile, your reviews and how close you are. The plain results below come mostly from your website.

Quick wins on the profile:

  • Main category: concrete contractor. Add secondary categories only for work you really do.
  • List services one by one: driveway installation, driveway replacement, patio, stamped concrete, exposed aggregate, slab, footings, steps, repairs.
  • Add the towns and suburbs you serve, not just your home town.
  • Post photos of real local jobs every week, with a short caption naming the area and job type.
  • Reply to every review, good or bad.

Our Google Business Profile checklist walks through every field. For reviews, see how to get Google reviews.

What should a concrete contractor website include?

One owner on r/Concrete recently asked what to include in a new website after 20 years, because the old one was "basically useless". It is a common problem. A homeowner comparing three quotes will check your site, and if it is one page that says "we do all concrete", you look smaller than you are.

A concrete website that wins jobs has:

  • A page for each job type, each with photos, what is included, rough timelines and the areas you cover. Google ranks pages, not businesses, so one page per service gives you a chance at each search.
  • A project gallery sorted by job type, with the suburb or town named.
  • Finish options shown clearly: broom, exposed aggregate, stamped patterns, colours, sealers. People often do not know the names until they see them.
  • Proof: licence, insurance, years in business, reviews, any trade body membership.
  • A short quote form that asks for the address, rough size, job type and photos of the area.
  • A phone number at the top that you can tap on a phone.

More detail is in our guide to what a trade website needs.

How do you use job photos to win concrete work?

Photos are the strongest selling tool you have, and most crews only take one shot at the end. Take five on every job:

  1. The old surface, cracked or sunken, from the street.
  2. The forms and reinforcement before the pour. This shows customers the work they will never see again.
  3. The pour and finishing, with your crew working.
  4. The finished surface, wide, in good light.
  5. A close up of the finish or pattern.

Use them on your Google profile, on the right service page of your website, in your quotes, and on Facebook or Instagram. A before and after pair of the same driveway from the same spot does more selling than any slogan. Ask the customer if you can name the suburb. Never show house numbers or number plates.

How do you get more driveway and patio jobs from one job?

Houses on the same street were usually built around the same time, so their driveways crack and sink at about the same age. When neighbours see a crew pouring a new drive, some of them start thinking about theirs. Before you start, knock on or leave a card at the houses either side and across the road:

"Hi, I'm Dan from [business]. We're replacing the driveway at number 22 this week, so you'll see a concrete truck on Tuesday morning. Sorry for any noise. If you've been thinking about your own driveway or patio, I'm happy to give you a free quote while we're on the street. Here's my card."

When the job is finished, drop a short card or flyer to the same houses with a photo of the new driveway. Some local Facebook groups and Nextdoor let businesses post finished work, but check each group's rules first.

Then send this text to the customer a week after the job: "Hi Karen, thanks again for choosing us for the driveway. If you're happy with it, a quick Google review would really help a small business like ours: [link]. And if any neighbours ask, feel free to pass on my number."

Should concrete contractors work for builders and other trades?

For many concrete businesses, steady trade work is the base and homeowner jobs are the margin. Builders need slabs, footings and paths on every house. Landscapers, pool builders, fencing companies and shed or garage suppliers all need concrete and often do not want to pour it themselves.

A simple message to send a local builder or landscaper:

"Hi Sarah, I run [business], a concrete crew based in [town]. We do slabs, footings, paths and driveways, and we turn up when we say we will. If you ever need a backup crew or a price on your next job, I'd be glad to quote. Photos of recent work are here: [link]."

Be clear about what you charge, pay terms and how far you will travel before you start. Our guides on getting work from builders and getting commercial work go deeper.

Are Google Ads and paid leads worth it for concrete contractors?

They can be, once your profile, website and photos are in place. Paid ads send people to your site, so a weak site wastes the money. Here are 2026 figures from US sources, so treat them as a guide, not a promise:

SourceReported 2026 cost per lead (USA)Notes
Google search ads for concreteAbout $35 to $165One marketing firm's 2026 concrete benchmarks. The low end came from a dedicated landing page, the high end from weak pages.
Google Local Services AdsAbout $50 to $53A Q1 2026 study of 3,367 leads put general contracting at $50.17. The firm above quotes about $53 for concrete.
Shared lead marketplacesVaries widelyThe same homeowner is often sent to several contractors, so close rates are lower.

On Reddit, concrete owners regularly ask whether what they pay for marketing is too much, and one recent thread asked whether 6.5% of job revenue was too high for lead generation. There is no fixed right answer. What matters is the cost per signed job. Here is the sum for one month, with example numbers to swap for your own:

StepExample
Ad spend$1,200
Leads18 (about $67 each)
Site visits and quotes9
Jobs signed3
Cost per signed job$1,200 / 3 = $400
Gross profit per jobYour number here

If $400 is a small slice of the profit on a driveway, keep going and raise the budget slowly. If small repair jobs are eating the budget, add negative keywords or switch the ads off for those terms. The same logic applies to Facebook ads. A plain "get your concrete quote" graphic tells people nothing, so use real before and after photos from local jobs, name the area and the job type, and track which ads lead to signed work.

In the UK, Checkatrade and similar directories are common for driveway work, and in Australia hipages is widely used. Both can work in the right area. Our guides on Checkatrade and Local Services Ads run the same sums.

How do concrete contractors get work in the off season?

Concrete lives and dies by the weather. Cold, wet weather slows or stops pours, and homeowners think about outdoor projects in spring. Plan your marketing a season ahead:

  • Late winter: push quotes for spring driveways and patios. Text past customers and anyone who got a quote last year.
  • Spring and summer: post finished jobs weekly, work the neighbours, ask for reviews.
  • Autumn: offer sealing, crack repair and step repair before winter, and book spring work early with a deposit.
  • Winter: indoor slabs, garage floors, polishing if you offer it, trade work for builders, and fixing your website and profile.

A text for past quotes in late winter: "Hi Tom, it's Dan from [business]. We quoted your driveway last year. We're booking spring pours now and have a few spots left in [month]. Want me to update the price for you?" See our slow season guide for more ways to fill quiet months.

Is concrete marketing different in the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand?

The basics are the same everywhere: a strong Google profile, local photos, reviews and fast replies. The local details change:

  • USA: stamped and decorative concrete are big sellers, and Local Services Ads are available in many areas.
  • UK: many people search for driveway contractors rather than concrete. In England, the Planning Portal says that paving more than five square metres of a front garden with a traditional impermeable surface needs planning permission unless rainwater runs to a lawn or border. Permeable options do not need it. Explaining this in a quote builds trust. This guide is general information, not legal or financial advice.
  • Canada: a short pouring season, frost and freeze thaw damage. Sell early spring bookings and repairs, and work builders through winter.
  • Australia and New Zealand: exposed aggregate and coloured concrete are common for driveways and outdoor areas, and the warmer months bring most enquiries.

blocks.title: Your checklist.
items: Set your Google Business Profile main category to concrete contractor and list every area you serve
Build one website page for each concrete job type, with local photos
Take five photos on every job, from the old surface to the clean finished site
Ask for a Google review on handover day and reply to every review
Leave a card with the neighbours before and after every pour
Send a short intro message with photos to three builders or landscapers this month
Track cost per signed job for every paid ad or lead source each month
Text last year's quotes in late winter to book spring work

items.q: How do concrete contractors get customers?
items.a: Most get work from Google searches, word of mouth from past customers and neighbours, and builders or landscapers who need a reliable crew. A complete Google profile, a website with job photos and steady reviews make all of those work better.

items.q: Is Google Ads worth it for a concrete business?
items.a: It can be once your website and photos are strong. 2026 benchmarks put concrete search ad leads at roughly $35 to $165 each in the USA. Track cost per signed job, and switch off searches that bring small repair jobs you do not want.

items.q: What should a concrete contractor post on social media?
items.a: Before and after photos of real local jobs, short videos of pours and finishing, and close ups of stamped or exposed finishes. Name the area and job type so people nearby know you work there.

items.q: How do I get more concrete driveway jobs?
items.a: Have a dedicated driveway page on your website, show finished local driveways on your Google profile, and leave a card with the neighbours around every driveway you pour. Streets often need new driveways around the same time.

items.q: How can a concrete company get work in winter?
items.a: Book spring work with deposits, offer sealing and repairs in autumn, and take indoor slabs, garage floors and builder work when outdoor pours slow down.

items.q: Do I need planning permission for a concrete driveway in the UK?
items.a: In England, a new or replacement front driveway over five square metres with an impermeable surface needs planning permission unless water drains to a lawn or border. Permeable surfaces do not. Check with the local council for your area.
